lifecycle.proof_status: READY_FOR_DEV: deferred reclaim-hardening follow-ups from MT-007 two-lens adversarial review.

origin: Deferred from MT-007 post-implementation adversarial review (2026-07-29).

scope.summary: Harden the spawned-process reclaim reaper beyond the MT-007 crash->restart boot case: cover the running-app window and decide fail-open vs fail-closed on kill failure. MT-007's blocker (generic reclaim wired into boot) is closed and runtime-proven; these are secondary residuals surfaced by adversarial review, deferred so they are not forgotten.
scope.root_cause: The boot reclaimer only surfaces dead-prior-owner (crash->restart) orphans; the periodic staleness task restart pass is disabled post-boot, and its stale_sessions query vetoes rows lacking a model_lanes record, so a live-instance official-CLI (no-lane) orphan is reaped only at the NEXT boot.
forbidden_paths: weakening any resolver fail-closed gate to make the loop close
acceptance_criteria: F1 (MAJOR): a same-instance mid-run official-CLI (no model_lanes row) orphan whose process terminated/reap-failed is reaped by the RUNNING app (staleness task or a CLI-session-end reclaim trigger), not only at next boot; add a runtime proof.

F2 (MAJOR): decide+implement the intended post-boot staleness restart-pass semantics (currently run_restart_pass=false) so restart-orphans get periodic re-surfacing if the boot pass is skipped/times out, OR document why boot-only suffices.

F3 (design decision, operator): kill-failure at boot is currently fail-OPEN (row left OPEN, boot continues). Decide resilient-boot (fail-open + retry) vs hard fail-closed (boot Err on un-reapable orphan); implement+prove the chosen contract incl. the non-Windows unavailable-adapter path (KillOutcome::Failed + row stays open).

F4 (MINOR): HANDSHAKE_STARTUP_RECOVERY_ONLY=1 returns before production_with_lease so it never surfaces generic spawned-process orphans; run reconcile_restart_orphans_at_boot in that branch too, or document the exclusion.

F5 (MINOR): reclaim.rs docstring/comment overstate fail-closed (true only for store/surfacing errors); RestartOrphanBootReconcileReport.processes_reclaimed counts KillOutcome::Failed as reclaimed. Correct the doc and count only Killed|KilledPendingStop (add processes_kill_failed).

F6 (MINOR): fold the staleness task inline restart loop (reclaim.rs ~4314) into reconcile_restart_orphans_at_boot with a caller-chosen error policy to prevent drift, OR document the intentional divergence; boot call site silently drops in-progress-reconcile sweep errors (ReclaimKillOperationSweep.reclaim_error).

F7 (NIT): MT-007 boot proof uses ProductionSandboxKill::new (default registry) and bypasses the production_with_lease 30s timeout wrapper; add coverage exercising with_registry(production_process_sandbox_registry()) + timeout. free_loopback_udp_port has an ephemeral-port re-bind flake window; retry or skip.
scope.risk_if_missed: A live-app official-CLI orphan can stay OPEN until the next restart; an un-reapable orphan is silently left open with an overstated fail-closed claim.

implementation_notes: Preferred direction (verify against spec + code before choosing): bind and cross-check on applied_update_id (identity) and verify the referenced kernel_crdt_updates row's OWN integrity (sha256(update_bytes)==update_sha256 + Update::decode_v1) independently, instead of requiring proposal.applied_update_sha256 to equal the Yjs update hash. The proposal's own content integrity (diff_sha256 over the JSON diff) stays a separate, still-enforced invariant.
Do NOT relax any resolver gate to make the loop close; the fix is to stop conflating two distinct hashes, not to drop a check.
Migration discipline: never edit 0192 in place; add a forward migration and document whether 0192's applied_update_sha256=diff_sha256 CHECK is superseded, retained, or replaced, with reasoning.

Build ONE reusable admissible-CRDT-message test helper (real persisted Yjs update + real base snapshot + active lease with matching actor/session/trace identity; update session_id == lane session_id; lease correlation_id == update trace_id) and use it for every positive CRDT admission proof so future tests stop hand-rolling partial/synthetic postures.
If this MT changes any product behavior, storage/event contract, or diagnostic surface, update the in-product UserManual in the same change per HBR-MAN-004.
Rust-only backend change plus governed migration; PostgreSQL/EventLedger authority only; no SQLite.

risks: A lazy fix drops the resolver cross-check entirely, admitting any proposal ref.
A migration edits 0192 in place and breaks historical applied-binding rows.
The reusable helper hard-codes an identity shortcut that a real caller could not reproduce, re-creating a scaffold-only proof.
minimum_controls: Keep every existing denial test green; add a negative test proving an internally inconsistent proposal row (JSON-hash != real update hash but pointed at a real update id) is still refused.
Forward-only migration with explicit 0192 disposition note.
Helper builds authority exclusively through real product APIs (apply_approved_ai_edit path or its governed equivalent), never by raw INSERT of an inconsistent row.

handshake_compatibility.spec_realism_gate: Implementer may move only to READY_FOR_VALIDATION after the three real-PG proof targets pass against the Handshake-managed cluster; COMPLETED is validator-only.
